# Vendored third-party code

Other authors' code, vendored in-tree — there is no package manager — and compiled into **both** app targets: `taglib/`, `PINCache/`, `PINOperation/`, `r8brain/`, `dr_mp3/`, `dr_flac/`, `dr_wav/`. **Do not restyle it.** Adding or removing a file means editing `project.yml` and re-running `xcodegen generate`.

Every component must be listed in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` at the repo root with the license it is used under. **TagLib is dual-licensed (LGPL 2.1 or MPL 1.1) and Vibe elects MPL 1.1** — that election is load-bearing, because TagLib is statically compiled into the app and the LGPL's static-linking obligation is incompatible with App Store distribution. Read that file before touching `taglib/`.

- **taglib** (a subset of TagLib 2.1.0, `toolkit/taglib.h`'s version) extracts audio metadata. Only the formats the app plays are vendored: `mpeg/` and ID3, `mp4/`, `flac/`, `riff/`, `ogg/` with its `vorbis/` and `opus/` files, plus the APE *tag* machinery MPEG files need and `ogg/xiphcomment` for FLAC and Ogg comments. Not Ogg FLAC, which the player refuses, and nothing for CAF or W64, which TagLib cannot read: their facts come from CoreAudio (`Audio/Metadata/AGENTS.md`). `TagLib::FileRef` is deliberately unused, since its detection references every format parser; `AudioTrackMetadata.mm` has a `TagLibAudioFile` factory that mirrors FileRef's extension-then-content-sniff detection for the supported formats. When updating, re-copy the subset and let the linker report anything new.
- **PINCache** and **PINOperation** provide disk and memory caching for metadata and waveform data. `PINDiskCache.m` is excluded from the recursive `ThirdParty` entry and re-added with a per-file `-fobjc-arc-exceptions` flag, as the pod's ARC-exception-safe subspec did. `make check-layout` whitelists that exclude, along with the `.xcprivacy`, `.txt` and `LICENSE.MPL` ones that keep license and privacy files out of the bundle — this directory is the only place file-level excludes are allowed at all.

- **r8brain** (r8brain-free-src, upstream commit `9e73d2dd`) is the voice bus's resampler (`Audio/AudioResampler.mm`). It is header-only apart from the two files `project.yml` excludes and re-adds with their own flags, `DLL/r8bsrc.cpp` (upstream's C entry points, where every template is instantiated) and `fft/pffft_double.c`: `-O3` in every configuration, since at `-O0` it would cost many times its optimized self and a Debug build is where its quality and cost tests run; `-DR8BSRC_DECL=` (upstream's switch from a DLL to an object file); `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`, the README's speed setting (double-precision PFFFT at Ooura's accuracy) — its other, `R8B_EXTFFT`, costs more than it saves at the 1% transition band `Audio/AudioResampler.mm` uses, so it is off (`docs/audio-quality.md`); and `PFFFT_ENABLE_NEON`. **TRAP: PFFFT's NEON path is opt-in, and `-w` hides the `#pragma message` that says so** — without the macro arm64 builds PFFFT's scalar fallback, 15–20% slower, with no error; x86_64 picks SSE2 by itself. Check with `clang -arch arm64 -fsyntax-only fft/pffft_double.c` plus the flags, which prints the backend chosen. `-w` silences the vendored C's warnings. Every file that includes an r8brain header must see the same `R8B_*` macros, so nothing but `r8bsrc.cpp` includes them. Upstream's `LICENSE` is vendored as `LICENSE.txt`, and the `.inc` filter tables are excluded, so neither is bundled. Only what those two files compile is vendored (checked with `clang -H` for arm64 and x86_64): not upstream's `r8butil.h`, the single-precision `pffft.c`, the Ooura `fft4g.h` (unused under `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`), the Windows DLL builds, `bench/` or `other/`. When updating, re-copy the same set and re-run that check.
- **dr_mp3** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_mp3 0.7.4) is `AudioFileHandle`'s default MPEG decoder (MP1, MP2, MP3), Apple's the alternative in the mac's Settings > Advanced (`docs/audio-quality.md`). Only its frame decoder (`drmp3dec_*`) is called: CoreAudio's parser still frames the packets. `dr_mp3.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, and defines `DR_MP3_FLOAT_OUTPUT` itself (its comment says why). `project.yml` excludes it and re-adds it with `-O3` in every configuration, for r8brain's reason, and `-w`. The license texts are at the end of the header. **`dr_mp3.h` is modified**: it carries two fixes on top of upstream, one commit each, the first two on the `vibe-mp3-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`, to be offered upstream (the branch's other three are upstream PRs that touch only the `drmp3` API Vibe does not call): MPEG-1 Layer III's private bits were read as the first granule's scfsi, so a frame with any set reused the scalefactors before it and misread the rest; and the 8 kHz row of `g_scf_mixed` (MPEG 2.5 mixed blocks) is now long bands 0–5 and short bands 3–12, as every other row is built, where upstream's reordered 600 lines, 24 floats past the granule, and scaled three bands by an earlier granule's scalefactors. When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`, whose `testDrMP3DecodesWhatAppleRoundsTo16Bits` holds the decode to Apple's, and whose `testDrMP3IgnoresPrivateBits` and `testDrMP3DecodesMixedBlocksAt8kHzAsFFmpegDoes` fail on upstream's copy.
- **dr_flac** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_flac 0.13.4) is `AudioFileHandle`'s FLAC decoder (`docs/audio-quality.md`). It reads the stream itself, through the handle's descriptor, after CoreAudio's parser has answered the file's facts. `dr_flac.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, with neither stdio nor Ogg, and builds with dr_mp3's flags. **`dr_flac.h` is modified too**: it carries fixes on top of upstream, one commit each, on the `vibe-flac-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`, whose tip it equals, to be offered upstream. The first nine: an ID3v2 tag in front of the stream (the metadata pass restarted at absolute byte 42); seeking past a frame whose first residual partition is empty (`drflac__read_and_seek_residual` had `<=` where the decoder has `<`); a stale seek table (the walk from a seekpoint trusted its sample number); a frame header that cannot belong to the stream ending the header search; the binary search rewritten to keep the target bracketed, since it could fall back to reading most of a file; damaged frames kept in the timeline as silence, as libFLAC does, while a frame cut short still ends the stream; a seek past the end of a truncated stream landing at its end; 32-bit streams, whose stereo side channel has 33 bits; and no clamp of a seek to an unknown (0) length. Then twelve from a review of those, with fuzzing and simulated damage: undefined behaviour in the 33-bit side channel, in a side channel that is all wasted bits, and in metadata parsing; a residual whose partitions don't divide the block; an Ogg page that failed its CRC read past; a frame that failed to decode leaving its samples behind (a crash reading a stream to its end and seeking back); a fixed block size stream's frame numbers counted in STREAMINFO's maximum block size; a false sync code written into the caller's frame header; a sync code right after a 0xFF byte missed; the bit streamer tracking its position and running out of data; seekpoints no stream could reach; and decoding and seeking kept in step through damage — a gap filled only before a frame that checks out, a failed frame looked past from its header, a cut frame told by the data running out, a damaged first frame, the brute-force and seek-table walks through the decoder's own code, a failed seek left at the first frame, and the binary search's probes bounded. Then one so a stream whose STREAMINFO leaves its length unknown (0), as an encoder that cannot seek back leaves it, is playable at all, since `AudioPlayer` refuses a length of 0: `drflac__find_unknown_total_pcm_frame_count`, at open, takes the end of the last frame that checks out, looked for from a frame's worth of bytes before the end of the stream and twice as far back each time none is found, so only the tail is read and bisection seeks work; a STREAMINFO allowing no block is not searched, since its window would never widen. Then two upstream bugs a review found: Rice partition orders past 8 were rejected as damage, in decoding, skipping and the 33-bit side channel, though only the streamable subset limits them (RFC 9639 sections 7 and 9.2.7); and the seek fast path cut its distance to 32 bits before checking it against the current frame, so a jump of 2^32 PCM frames or more landed inside that frame. And five for speed, which halve the decode's cycles on Apple Silicon: the CRC-16 eight bytes at a time; the NEON f32 conversions, and the SSE2 ones, made to agree with the scalar ones outside the bit depth; a NEON residual decoder of Vibe's own, since upstream's was slower than its own scalar one there; and `drflac_read_pcm_frames_f32_planar`, which `AudioFileHandle`'s planar reads call, writing each channel straight to its own buffer. `dr_flac.c` keeps NEON on: `DR_FLAC_NO_SIMD` costs 20% more cycles now. When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`: `testDrFLACDecodesWhatTheFileHolds`, `testDrFLACSurvivesWhatDamagesFiles` and `testDrFLACSeeksFurtherThanThirtyTwoBitsOfFrames` fail on upstream's copy. They check what decodes and seeks deliver, and what seeks cost only near a garbage seekpoint, so a copy that seeks slowly again, as upstream's search could for seconds on a long file, passes them.
- **dr_wav** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_wav 0.14.6-dev) is `AudioFileHandle`'s WAV, W64, RF64 and AIFF(-C) decoder of integer and float PCM, A-law, mu-law and ADPCM (`docs/audio-quality.md`). It reads the stream itself, through the handle's descriptor and the same callbacks as dr_flac, after CoreAudio's parser has answered the file's facts. `dr_wav.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, without stdio, and builds with dr_mp3's flags; `DRWAV_MAX_SAMPLE_RATE` stays upstream's 384 kHz, so a faster file is Apple's. **`dr_wav.h` is modified**: 24 commits on top of upstream, one each, on the `vibe-wav-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`, to be offered upstream. Fixes: an AIFF's SSND offset and block size fields counted as audio (forward seeks landed late in any AIFF with a chunk after SSND); AIFF-C A-law and mu-law bytes shifted as signed 8-bit samples; unsigned 8-bit silence converted to 1/255; a COMM, fact or ds64 count trusted past the data; PCM seeks placed from the frame count less the bytes remaining, and a seek past 2 GB stepping in `INT_MAX` bytes, a partial frame each; data sizes of 0, 0xFFFFFFFF or wrapped past 4 GB (the 0xFFFFFFFF recount read from the end of the file); an IMA ADPCM block cut short counted by bytes, not groups, and an MS ADPCM one by a whole header however little of it was there; COMM chunks of 23 bytes, odd size or more than 18; a fmt chunk after the data; four chunk sizes that hung the open, and a long seek with no `onTell`, found by fuzzing; the MS ADPCM sample update overflowing; a damaged ADPCM block ending the stream or dropping out of the timeline, now silence in its place; W64 padding; the MS ADPCM fact count never used; the AIFF rate's 80-bit conversion overflowing; WAV ADPCM block sizes that cannot decode; and an MS ADPCM coefficient table other than the standard seven, the only one the decoder has, now refused, so CoreAudio decodes it. Additions: AIFF-C twos, in24, in32, 42ni, 23ni and ima4, ima4 carrying its predictor across packets as CoreAudio does, with decoder states kept every 64 packets for exact seeks. And four for speed: PCM, float and G.711 read straight into the f32 output and converted in place with NEON or SSE2, every value the scalar one; `drwav_read_pcm_frames_f32_planar`, which `AudioFileHandle`'s planar reads call, converting stereo straight into a buffer a channel with NEON; ADPCM read ahead 16 KB at a time; and ADPCM seeks from the block holding the target. When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`: `testDrWAVDecodesAsAppleDoes` and `testDrWAVSurvivesWhatDamagesFiles` fail on upstream's copy.

`ThirdParty/` is excluded from `make analyze` and from every other check in the repo, on the same grounds: it is not ours to fix.

Framework-style imports such as `<PINCache/...>` resolve through the shared `vibe-header-paths` setting group in `project.yml`, which both app targets use so a second platform cannot drift from the first.
